headline_marked: [[Cisco launches free tool]] to verify lineage of almost 900 open AI models, 69% previously unverified
headline: Cisco launches free tool to verify lineage of almost 900 open AI models, 69% previously unverified
summary: Cisco's new AI Supply Chain Provenance Explorer offers a free public database to verify the lineage, license restrictions, and scan coverage of almost 900 open AI models, addressing a critical security gap.
details: A significant security gap exists in the open-source AI ecosystem, with 69% of open models' lineage unverified, relying solely on self-reported tags by uploaders on platforms like Hugging Face. As of February 2026, Alibaba’s Qwen family is the declared parent of 69% of new open-model derivatives, up from 1% in January 2024.

Cisco has released the AI Supply Chain Provenance Explorer, a free public database covering almost 900 open models. This tool provides crucial data including provider headquarters, a fingerprinted lineage graph, license restrictions, and a files-scanned count for each entry.

The Explorer extends Cisco’s Model Provenance Kit, an open-source Python toolkit, which previously required local environments and significant engineering effort. The new tool queries pre-computed results, making verification accessible via a simple search bar.

The verification process employs a two-stage method, first comparing architecture metadata and then extracting five weight-level signals when metadata is ambiguous. This methodology achieves 96.4% accuracy in identifying model relationships, grounding them in similarity scores rather than self-reported metadata.

Amy Chang, head of AI Threat Intelligence and Security Research at Cisco, emphasized the importance of verification, citing high success rates in multi-turn attacks against flagship models. Understanding model vulnerabilities starts with knowing the true origin and characteristics of the models being used.
